chara_procedure: Take the eight planets – Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn and Rahu. For each planet, find its advancement from the beginning of the rasi occupied by it. For Rahu, measure the advancement from the end of his rasi.
Arrange them in the decreasing order of advancement.
The planet with the highest advancement is Atma Karaka (significator of self). We will denote him by AK. Find other chara karakas using Table 13.

chara_table.name: Atma Karaka
chara_table.note: throws light on the inner self of a native

chara_table.name: Amatya Karaka
chara_table.note: in practical terms, people who give advice — advisors and counsellors

chara_table.name: Putra Karaka
chara_table.note: can also show subordinates and followers

chara_table.name: Jnaati Karaka
chara_table.note: commonly used for enemies or rivals; the literal meaning of 'jnaati' is 'paternal cousin'

body.chara_tie_break: If two planets have the same degrees, we should compare minutes. If minutes are same, we should compare the seconds.

choosing.question: birth of children, or simple events from their lives
children-related troubles that punish one's soul, or achievements and happiness related to children
timing the death of a child

body.definition: Karaka of a matter is the significator of the matter. He is the one who causes events related to that matter.
body.jnaati_pronunciation: In 'jn', 'j' is the voiced palatal consonant and 'n' is the palatal nasal. A tough sound to pronounce correctly; some approximate it as 'gnaati' or 'gyaati'.

kinds.name: Naisargika karaka
kinds.presiding_because: Brahma is the creator of everything that exists
kinds.read_as_note: Take the relevant house counted from the karaka, not the karaka himself: the 7th from Venus shows husband, not Venus
kinds.shows: everything that exists in Brahma's creation and affects a person, impersonal things and matters included
kinds.shows_contrast: Naisargika karakas show not only human beings, but they show various impersonal things and matters.
kinds.used_for: phalita jyotish — analysis of general results

kinds.also_shows: how our karma (cumulative sum of actions) is carried from one life to another

excludes.reason: Ketu stands for moksha (emancipation) and does not stand for any person who affects one's sustenance

kinds.name: Chara karaka
kinds.presiding_because: Vishnu presides over activities related to sustenance, achievements and spiritual progress
kinds.read_as_note: The karaka himself shows the matter: DK himself shows spouse, not the 7th from DK
kinds.shows: people who play an important role in one's sustenance and achievements
kinds.shows_broadly: people who play a role in one's life

kinds.also_shows: the destruction of the body, as Shiva presides over death

excludes.reason: only the seven have physical bodies
only the seven have physical bodies

kinds.name: Sthira karaka
kinds.read_as_note: The karaka himself represents the relative's physical body: Jupiter is the husband's body in a female chart
kinds.used_for: timing the death of various near relatives

body.shared_karakatwa: Two grahas at exactly the same longitude hold a karakatwa together and the next karakatwa has no ruler; use the corresponding sthira karaka. This rarely becomes necessary, as two planets are rarely at exactly the same longitude.

usage_rules.because: Venus is the natural significator of marriage, and the 7th from Venus applies in both male and female charts
usage_rules.right: the 7th from Venus to predict marriage
usage_rules.rule: Sthira karakas should not be used in general predictive astrology in the place of naisargika karakas
usage_rules.wrong: the 7th from Jupiter to predict marriage

usage_rules.because: sthira karakas represent physical bodies; Jupiter is the husband's body, while the 7th from Venus is what shows the husband for timing marriage
usage_rules.right: Jupiter for the death of a husband in a female chart
usage_rules.rule: Use the sthira karaka only for timing death, where the karaka is the relative's body
usage_rules.wrong: Venus for the death of a husband in a female chart

body.warning: One should not use the three types of karakas in a mixed-up way. Karakas of each type have a specific purpose. One should understand the distinction between chara, sthira and naisargika karakas clearly and use them accordingly.
